key_insight: Robot demonstrations can teach task steps and object roles—not just visual patterns. This semantic understanding offers a way to transfer manipulation experience between scenes without encoding every skill in network weights.
problem_solved: Trained robot policies are tied to their training distribution, while conventional in-context demonstrations lack feedback from the robot’s current environment, limiting adaptation.
method: Use in-context experience to guide manipulation rather than relying solely on skills stored in trained policy weights.
Focus on semantic information—task sequences and object roles—rather than scene-specific appearance. The supplied abstract is truncated, so the complete mechanism is not available.
impact: The approach points toward robot agents that reuse experience across changing environments with less dependence on task-specific training. Performance gains and implementation details cannot be assessed from the provided excerpt.

paper_title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang, Mingyang Du, Dingkang Liang
